s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painless nodules with vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts on the fingers, with associated arm and forearm discomfort
salient_findings: Vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
Discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of the right arm and forearm
key_facts: 30-year-old male
Dairy farm worker
Multiple painless nodules on fingers of both hands
Nodules appeared 1 month prior to presentation
Vesicles developed 7-10 days after initial nodules
Hemorrhagic crusts formed after vesicle rupture
Discomfort and pain along the medial right arm and forearm
Denies trauma or insect bites
Cow had similar lesions on its teats
3-4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema on proximal phalanges of both hands
Mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm

shortlist.label: Orf virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of painless nodules with vesicles and hemorrhagic crusts, and the patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker

shortlist.label: Milker's nodule
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Orf virus infection, it matches the clinical presentation and the patient's occupation

shortlist.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Also known as cowpox or pseudocowpox, it is a zoonotic disease that can cause similar lesions in humans and animals

shortlist.label: Erysipeloid
shortlist.why_kept: A zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions and is associated with animal contact

shortlist.label: Pseudocowpox
shortlist.why_kept: A viral infection that can cause similar lesions to those described in the case, and is associated with contact with infected animals

raw.rationale: The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on the cow's teats, along with the characteristic skin lesions, are highly suggestive of Milker's nodule, which is caused by Paravaccinia virus but the term Milker's nodule is more specific to the context provided.

rejected.label: Orf virus infection
rejected.why: While Orf virus infection can cause similar lesions, it is more commonly associated with direct contact with infected sheep, goats, or their products, and the context of cow lesions is less typical.

rejected.label: Paravaccinia virus infection
rejected.why: Although Paravaccinia virus is the causative agent of Milker's nodule, the term 'Milker's nodule' is more specific and directly related to the patient's occupation and the nature of the lesions.

rejected.label: Erysipeloid
rejected.why: Erysipeloid is an infection caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, typically presenting with well-demarcated, erythematous lesions, often on the hands, but it doesn't typically start with nodules and vesicles as described.

rejected.label: Pseudocowpox
rejected.why: Pseudocowpox, caused by the Paravaccinia virus, presents similarly but the term 'Milker's nodule' is more specific to the context of dairy workers and the lesions' characteristics.
